title: Private Lander Carrying NASA Experiments Lands on the Moon
titleZh: 私人着陆器搭载NASA实验设备成功登月
credits: The Associated Press, Agence France-Presse and NASA reported on this story. Bryan Lynn adapted the reports for VOA Learning English.

sentences.en: A private spacecraft carrying several science experiments has successfully landed on the moon.
sentences.zh: 一艘搭载多项科学实验的私人航天器已成功登月。

sentences.en: The lander, called Blue Ghost, was built by the American company Firefly Aerospace.
sentences.zh: 这艘着陆器名为"蓝幽灵"，由美国萤火虫航天公司建造。

sentences.en: The spacecraft touched down March 2 on the part of the moon’s near side called Mare Crisium.
sentences.zh: 该航天器于3月2日降落在月球正面被称为"风暴洋"的区域。

sentences.en: The near side of the moon is the side facing Earth.
sentences.zh: 月球正面是朝向地球的一面。

sentences.en: Officials at Firefly’s Mission Control center near Austin, Texas, confirmed the successful landing.
sentences.zh: 位于得克萨斯州奥斯敦附近的萤火虫任务控制中心官员证实了此次成功着陆。

sentences.en: The chief engineer for the Blue Ghost mission, Will Coogan, announced to excited workers: “We’re on the moon.”
sentences.zh: 蓝幽灵任务的首席工程师威尔·科根向兴奋的工作人员宣布："我们登月了。"

sentences.en: The officials said the spacecraft landed in the right position and was operating normally.
sentences.zh: 官员表示，航天器降落在正确位置，运行正常。

sentences.en: The successful touchdown makes Firefly the first private company to land a spacecraft on the moon without crashing or having a major problem.
sentences.zh: 此次成功着陆使萤火虫成为首家将航天器成功登月而未坠毁或出现重大问题的私人公司。

sentences.en: Only five countries can claim successful moon landings: Russia, the United States, China, India and Japan.
sentences.zh: 目前只有五个国家宣称成功登月：俄罗斯、美国、中国、印度和日本。

sentences.en: Blue Ghost is named after a rare kind of firefly found in the U.S. The four-legged lander is two meters tall and 3.5 meters wide.
sentences.zh: 蓝幽灵得名于美国一种罕见的萤火虫。这艘四条腿的着陆器高2米，宽3.5米。

sentences.en: It launched in mid-January from Florida, carrying 10 experiments for the American space agency NASA.
sentences.zh: 它于1月中旬从佛罗里达州发射升空，搭载美国国家航空航天局（NASA）的10项实验。

sentences.en: In a statement, NASA said the 10 experiments are designed to operate on the surface of the moon for one lunar day, which is about 14 Earth days.
sentences.zh: NASA在一份声明中表示，这10项实验设计用于在月球表面运行一个朔望月，约等于14个地球日。

sentences.en: The Associated Press reported that NASA paid $101 million for the spacecraft and $44 million for the equipment it carried.
sentences.zh: 美联社报道，NASA为这艘航天器支付了1.01亿美元，为其搭载的设备支付了4400万美元。

sentences.en: It was the third mission under NASA’s Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) program.
sentences.zh: 这是NASA商业月球有效载荷服务（CLPS）项目的第三次任务。

sentences.en: The program aims to turn over the country’s major space missions to private companies to reduce costs.
sentences.zh: 该项目旨在将国家重大太空任务交给私人公司，以降低成本。

sentences.en: Several other companies are part of the program.
sentences.zh: 其他几家公司也参与了该项目。

sentences.en: Another lander, called Athena, is set to attempt a moon landing on March 6.
sentences.zh: 另一艘名为"雅典娜"的着陆器计划于3月6日尝试登月。

sentences.en: That four-meter-tall spacecraft was built and operated by Houston-based Intuitive Machines.
sentences.zh: 这艘高4米的航天器由位于休斯顿的直觉机器公司建造并运营。

sentences.en: It will land on another part of the moon, about 160 kilometers from the lunar south pole.
sentences.zh: 它将降落在月球另一区域，距离月球南极约160公里。

sentences.en: A third lander from private Japanese company ispace will attempt a moon landing in about three months.
sentences.zh: 第三艘着陆器来自日本私人公司ispace，计划在约三个月后尝试登月。

sentences.en: The lander, called Resilience, shared its rocket ride with Blue Ghost.
sentences.zh: 着陆器名为'韧性号'，与'蓝色幽灵号'共用同一枚火箭升空。

sentences.en: But it took a longer path to the moon.
sentences.zh: 但它选择了更漫长的登月之路。

sentences.en: The company is also attempting to land on the moon for the second time.
sentences.zh: 该公司也正试图第二次实现登月。

sentences.en: Its first lander crashed in 2023.
sentences.zh: 它的首个着陆器在2023年坠毁。

sentences.en: NASA has said it aims to have two private landers launch to the moon each year, realizing some missions will fail.
sentences.zh: 美国国家航空航天局表示，其目标是每年发射两艘私人着陆器登月，并承认部分任务会失败。

sentences.en: The space agency’s top science officer is Nicky Fox.
sentences.zh: 美国国家航空航天局的首席科学官员是妮基·福克斯。

sentences.en: She told the AP the latest launches “open up a whole new way for us to get more science to space and to the moon."
sentences.zh: 她告诉美联社，最新的发射'为我们开辟了一条全新的途径，让我们能够向太空和月球输送更多科学成果。'

sentences.en: In the past, NASA’s successful moon landings involving astronauts cost billions of dollars.
sentences.zh: 在过去，涉及宇航员的美国国家航空航天局成功登月任务耗资数十亿美元。

sentences.en: But Firefly chief Jason Kim said the private companies now building and launching spacecraft have a limited budget and the spacecraft operate robotically.
sentences.zh: 但萤火虫公司首席运营官金智贤表示，如今正在建造和发射航天器的私人公司预算有限，且航天器以机器人方式运行。

sentences.en: Kim said everything went just as planned with Blue Ghost’s landing.
sentences.zh: 金说，'蓝色幽灵号'的着陆一切按计划进行。

sentences.en: “We got some moon dust on our boots," he added.
sentences.zh: 他补充道：'我们的靴子上沾了一些月球尘埃。'

sentences.en: I’m Bryan Lynn.
sentences.zh: 我是布莱恩·林恩。

glossary.def: (space exploration) the flight of a spacecraft to its target along with tasks expected to be carried out
